title: Paystride Instant Pay Disbursement Service — Fee Credit Rules for the Billing Desk
content:
**The rules.** The per-disbursement fee of an instant external payout on the Paystride Instant Pay Disbursement Service whose delivery minutes exceed the tier's instant external delivery time is credited with reason late delivery when the tier credits late instant fees, without a request. A fee debited in error is credited in full with reason fee charged in error. A correct fee may be credited as a courtesy only while the number of courtesy fee credits in the 365 calendar days ending today is below the tier's courtesy allowance. A fee is credited only when the credit is raised within the tier's fee credit request window in calendar days of the fee's entry date. Calendar days are counted from the day after the fee's entry date, so the last day to ask is the entry date plus the window. Late-delivery credits are raised on delivery and fall inside that window; a fee not questioned within it is deemed accepted and is not credited for any reason. A fee is credited at most once. A credit always returns the whole fee and points to it.

The fee's entry date is read from the fee entry on the service's ledger, found by its reference; whether the fee has already been credited is read from the credits pointing to it.

## Questions the rules answer

**Is a late-delivery credit asked for by the employer?** No; it is credited without a request, with reason late delivery.

**May part of a fee be credited?** No. A credit always returns the whole fee.

**A fee was booked on day D and the window is 30 days. Until when can a credit be raised?** Through day D plus 30. A credit raised on day D plus 30 is in time; one raised on day D plus 31 is outside the window, and the fee is deemed accepted.

**With a 60-day window, is day D plus 60 still in time?** Yes; the last day to ask is the entry date plus the window, and that day is included.

**On a tier with a courtesy allowance of 1, may a courtesy credit be given when one courtesy credit was booked 200 days ago?** No; 1 courtesy credit in the 365 days ending today is not below 1. Once that credit is more than 365 days old the count is 0, which is below 1.

**May a fee be credited twice for two different reasons?** No; a fee is credited at most once.
